target_customer: Independent fitness, yoga and wellness studio owners and instructors who pay a monthly software fee
problem: Small studios and instructors had to stitch together booking, payments, video on demand and website tools, or pay for heavyweight legacy studio software.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment processing fees
product_category: Fitness and wellness studio management software

founders.name: Rachel Lea Fishman
founders.background_notes: YC page describes her as a yoga instructor and group fitness fan. Prior employers not listed.

founders.name: Josh Archer
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an Ironman triathlete. The company's seed post calls him an engineer. Education and prior employers not found.

competitors.name: Mindbody
competitors.what: Dominant legacy booking and payments software for fitness and wellness studios
competitors.traction_then: Market leader with thousands of studio customers, per later third party profiles

competitors.name: Mariana Tek
competitors.what: Boutique fitness studio software focused on enterprise and franchise studios

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, payments, video on demand and website hosting are standard web engineering. The hard parts were breadth of features and payments integration for a two person founding team.

defensibility.rationale: Studios store schedules, client lists and payment data in the product, which creates modest switching costs, but many vendors offered similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mindbody remained a larger rival and no incumbent bought or copied Arketa through 2025 based on the sources found.

market_need_then: The 2020 pandemic forced studios to move classes online and sell video on demand, creating sudden demand for low cost all in one tools. The seed post says thousands of studios were using the product by late 2022.

branding.name_origin: The company's Nov 2023 post says Arketa is a Greek derived word meaning enough, chosen to tell fitness pros that their effort is enough.
branding.domain_note: arketa.com in use by 2023 after the rename; earlier domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and encouraging toward instructors, per the rename post

branding.brand_signature: The meaning enough, used as an affirmation for wellness professionals

rebrands.why: Company says Arketa was a better fit for its community as the business grew

brand_strength.rationale: Only the company's own rename post was found. No press about the brand or community evidence. The company operated as Sutra for its first three years, so the brand is young.

outcome_analysis: Arketa started in the 2020 pandemic, when studios suddenly needed online class and video on demand tools, and grew into an all in one platform. It raised a $7.6M seed in late 2022 and a $15M Series A in June 2025, renamed from Sutra Fitness in November 2023, and was still active with about 55 people. No shutdown or sale was found. Evidence of strong product market fit is thin beyond the company's own claims.
notes: Company website arketa.com was reached only through its blog pages. Seed date: the company blog page fetched showed an April 2024 date, but Fitt Insider dated the story 13 Dec 2022 and aggregators say Dec 2022, so 2022-12 is used. The seed amount is $7.6M per Fitt Insider and the blog, while one outlet said $7.5M. Aggregators gave total funding of $23M and $33.2M, unverified. Competitor entries come from a rival's current comparison page and are undated, so they are not confirmed as of 2020. Funding search also showed a 'Series A $18M' aggregator headline, unverified.
